title: Quarterly Executive Connection Kit
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, repeatable kit for Customer Success managers to run an executive-facing quarterly connection (QBR-style) with an Executive Sponsor. It is intentionally concise: one short pre-read email, a 20–30 minute executive touchpoint agenda, a slim slide outline for the customer-facing deck, and a follow-up template that feeds directly into renewal tracking and cadence planning.

When to use:
- Quarterly or renewal-adjacent check-ins with the named Executive Sponsor
- Early signs of adoption or ROI stalls where executive-level unblockers may accelerate outcomes
- Renewal conversations where the sponsor needs a concise recap to brief internal procurement/stakeholders

Audience:
Primary: Executive Sponsor (VP+), Secondary: CS Lead, Solutions Architect, Customer Success Manager (CSM)

Pre-meeting checklist (owner: CSM, complete >= 72h before):
- Confirm sponsor's preferred length and participants (20 vs 30 min).
- Attach 1-page pre-read (PDF) summarizing metrics and asks.
- Run a quick health read: usage last 90 days, key features used, top 3 incidents/tickets.
- Fresh renewal status: committed, likelihood (high/med/low), renewal date, contract owner.
- Prepare one concise ask (e.g., approval for expanded sandbox, sign-off for pilot extension).
- Slack/Email DM to internal exec sponsor counterpart to align on meeting outcomes.

Pre-read (single page) - sections to include (one-line each):
- One-sentence value recap: what the customer got this quarter (ex: 27% faster inference at 40% lower cost using Redwood Dedicated).
- Top metric snapshot (3 KPIs): latency P50/P95, cost per 1k tokens, active routes.
- Adoption highlights: 2 short bullets (new teams on platform, features enabled).
- Risk & ask: one-line risk and the single requested executive action.
- Next milestone: renewal date or target deployment milestone.

Suggested meeting agenda (20 minutes):
1) 0:00–0:02 — Quick hellos and outcome framing (CSM)
2) 0:02–0:08 — Business outcomes snapshot (CS lead): metrics and impact on product/ops
3) 0:08–0:12 — Recent wins & blockers (SA/CSM): what helped, what’s stuck
4) 0:12–0:18 — Executive ask & decision (CSM): one specific ask; options presented
5) 0:18–0:20 — Wrap and next steps ownership

Alternative 30-minute flow (adds 1–2 mins Q&A and a brief roadmap alignment slot).

Slide deck outline (3–6 slides, keep minimal):
- Slide 1: Title + meeting objectives + one-line value statement
- Slide 2: KPI snapshot (3 x tiles with trend sparkline)
- Slide 3: Customer adoption highlights (teams / routes / features) + one quote / internal reference
- Slide 4: Risks & mitigation plan (incidents, capacity, costs)
- Slide 5: Executive ask & options (decision needed, timeline)
- Slide 6: Next steps & owners + renewal timeline

Email templates (short, customizable). Use {{placeholders}} when preparing copy.

1) Pre-read invite (48–72h before) — Subject options:
- "Quick Q1 check-in: {{customer_company}} + Redwood — 20 min"
- "Proposed 20-min exec recap before {{renewal_month}}"

Body:
Hi {{executive_name}},

I want to share a short update on how {{customer_company}} is getting value from Redwood and surface one small executive decision that would unblock faster scale. Would you be open to 20 minutes on {{proposed_date}}? I’ll send a one-page pre-read and a crisp options slide; goal is a quick alignment so your team can keep momentum.

If yes, I’ll attach the pre-read and keep to a strict 20-min agenda.
Thanks,
{{cs_owner}}

2) Follow-up — meeting confirmation with pre-read (immediately after scheduling)
Subject: "Confirmed: 20-min update — {{company}} + Redwood (pre-read attached)"

Body:
Thanks, {{executive_name}} — confirmed for {{meeting_time}}. Attaching a one-page pre-read. TL;DR: improved throughput, a capacity ask, and a renewal milestone in {{renewal_month}}.
See you then — I’ll keep it to 20 minutes.

3) Post-meeting recap email (send same day) — Subject:
- "Recap + decision items — {{company}} executive update with Redwood"

Body:
Hi {{executive_name}},

Thanks for the time today. Short recap:
- Outcome: {{one_line_outcome}}
- Agreed action: {{decision}} (owner: {{owner}} by {{date}})
- Risks to watch: {{risk_1}}, {{risk_2}}
Next steps: we’ll follow up with a milestones email and add the renewal checkpoint to your calendar for {{renewal_month}}.

If helpful, I’ll prepare a one-page status for procurement.
Best,
{{cs_owner}}

Renewal tracker row (single-line format for spreadsheet import):
- Customer: {{company_name}} | Exec Sponsor: {{executive_name}} | Renewal date: {{YYYY-MM-DD}} | Renewal status: {Committed/Negotiating/AtRisk} | Current ARR: {{amount}} | Likelihood: {High/Med/Low} | Next exec action: {{action}} | Owner: {{cs_owner}} | Last touched: {{last_touch_date}}

Risk signals (watch these, escalate early):
- 30%+ drop in route volume month-over-month
- Sudden spike in P95 latency without configuration change
- Increased repeat support tickets around a single integration point
- Procurement delays or procurement reassignments
- Usage plateau with no roadmap alignment request from the customer

How to surface to Sales/RevOps/AM (if renewal or expansion impacted):
- Create a quick one-pager: 1-line update, metric delta, ask + suggested executive contact
- Post in #renewals-alerts with the one-pager and tag the named AM/AE
- Book a 15-min sync with AE + RevOps to align contract levers and timing

Ownership & escalation matrix (short):
- CSM: owner of pre-read, meeting logistics, post-meeting recap
- Solutions Architect: short technical summary and mitigation options for risk items
- Account Executive: commercial negotiations & procurement interface
- CS Lead (manager): escalate if Likelihood=Low or Risk signals present

Checklist for capturing the meeting in the CRM (immediately after):
- Update customer health score and renewal likelihood
- Attach the one-page pre-read and slide deck to the account record
- Enter the decision/action next steps with due dates and owners
- Move renewal tracker row to next stage if decision made

Templates for single-sentence personalization (pick 1):
- "Noticed adoption grew in the payments route — great early win for latency-sensitive flows."
- "Your infra team reported a 3x reduction in warmup time after the caching change we deployed."
- "Wanted to highlight that the procurement timeline aligns well with your FY planning in {{renewal_month}}."

Metrics to pull for the KPI snapshot (metric name | preferred time window):
- Active routes | 90d
- P50 latency (ms) | 30d
- P95 latency (ms) | 30d
- Cost per 1k tokens or cost per 1000 invocations | 30d
- % traffic using cached responses | 14d
- Incidents (SEV2+) | 90d

Example single-line executive ask phrasing (pick 1):
- "Approve a 6-week pilot to add Redwood Dedicated capacity for core production routes to reduce 95th percentile latency by approx. 20%."
- "Sign-off to allocate a cross-functional executive sponsor for procurement to approve the renewal by {{renewal_month}}."

Notes on tone and brevity:
- Keep emails and slides highly outcome-focused: execs want impact, decision(s), and proposed next steps.
- Avoid deep technical detail in the exec touchpoint; offer the SA for a follow-up technical deep-dive.

Quick examples (realistic short snippets):
Pre-read TL;DR: "In Q4 we reduced model cost by 33% via quantization on non-latency-critical routes; P95 latency for core checkout route improved from 720ms to 550ms. We’re requesting a pilot of Dedicated capacity to lower P95 further. Renewal: 2026-09-15."

Post-meeting action item template (copy into Jira or Linear):
Title: "Exec decision: Pilot Dedicated capacity for checkout route"
Description: "Sponsor approved 6-week pilot to validate P95 improvement and cost impact. SA to scope nodes; CSM to coordinate procurement."
Assignee: {{owner}}
Due: {{date}}

Version notes / playbook updates: 2026-03 — condensed to one-page pre-read; added renewal tracker row template and explicit risk signals list per CS leadership feedback.

Open questions & follow-ups (for CS team):
- Should we create a deck variant specifically for renewal-only meetings? (yes/no)
- Default CC list for exec invite: include AE, CS Lead, SA — confirm with the Executive Sponsor preference.

End of kit. Use this as a copy-paste working template for calendar invites, one-pagers, and the CRM. Keep each exec touchpoint lightweight and focused on a single decision to increase closure velocity.
